newsitem.title: CHINA: It's a HK bestseller -- and it's free.
newsitem.headline: It's a HK bestseller -- and it's free.

text.p: The hottest item in Hong Kong on Tuesday was penned by its new leader, Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa.
Tens of thousands of people queued up in the concourses of the underground railway system for free copies of the speech unveiling Tung's political agenda.

Tung made the speech after taking over as head of Hong Kong when it reverted to Chinese rule at midnight on Monday. Only hours after being sworn in as chief executive, Tung was clearly out to make his mark.

His speech went straight to the heart of Hong Kong's entrepreneurial populace. He said his aim was to achieve a home ownership rate of 70 percent in 10 years in the territory which has some of the world's most pricey real estate.
Other than that the prevailing theme was in line with Hong Kong's businesslike approach to life.
"Our foremost task is to enhance Hong Kong's economic vitality and sustain economic growth," Tung said. "Only through the creation of wealth can we improve the living of the people of Hong Kong."
